title: Fourier coefficients of a difference
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by $\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For functions $f,g:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$ and a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient of $f-g$ at $a$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$ minus the Fourier coefficient of $g$ at $a$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite, nonempty, and has decidable equality
The basis is indexed by $\iota$ and spans the real-valued functions on $\Omega$
The basis vector at the distinguished index is constant $1$
